newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid bourse sinks lower on Wall Street losses.
newsitem.headline: Madrid bourse sinks lower on Wall Street losses.

text.p: The Madrid bourse sunk lower into the close on Monday, depressed by losses on Wall Street and European markets. Dealers pointed out that movements had been exaggerated in thin summer trade.
The general index closed down 8.89 points, 1.50 pct, to 583.72, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares fell 104.63 points, 1.55 pct, to 6,625.85. Turnover reached a meagre 63.7 billion pesetas.

"Flows to funds have dropped off and we are paying for sharp rises in previous months," said one dealer. "I think these falls bode well for the medium term as the Ibex has already lost close to 600 points since recent highs."
Dealers said the market had been unsettled by worries over possible hikes in interest rates in the United States and possibly Germany.
Among individual stocks, Telefonica, the most actively traded share, ended 70 pesetas down at 3,990. Repsol, the second most actively traded share, fell 110 pesetas to 6,100.

Iberdrola ended five pesetas up at 1,760. An Iberdrola-lead consortium won a controlling stake in Brazilian power distributor Coelba last week. "Iberdrola is still gaining from the Coelba purchase," said one dealer.
